findings.heading: File size
findings.proposition: Shrinking the interactive plot's data size has no negative side effects in most cases. The English states this as a reassurance in parentheses; the Spanish instead instructs the reader to prevent negative repercussions wherever possible, which asserts that the reader must manage downsides the English says are usually absent.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader treats partial_bundle() as a trade-off needing active mitigation, and may hesitate to apply it or waste time looking for side effects that the English says normally do not occur.

findings.heading: Plot with `ggplotly()`
findings.proposition: The last modebar control adjusts WHETHER data are shown when the cursor is not hovering on the line, i.e. it is a toggle with both states. The Spanish states the control makes the data show when the cursor is not on the line, describing only one state.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader expects a single-purpose button that always displays data, and does not understand that the control switches the hover-comparison behaviour on and off.

findings.heading: Load packages
findings.proposition: `library()` comes from base R. The English attributes the function to base R; the Spanish names `library()` with no attribution.
findings.reader_consequence: A Spanish reader loses the contrast the sentence is built on, that `p_load()` needs the pacman package while `library()` needs no package at all, and may look for a package to install before using `library()`.
